config.title: Race Condition Fix

intro.title: Race Condition Fix
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that fetches and displays user data, and learn how to fix a common race condition bug. You will understand how race conditions occur when multiple asynchronous requests compete, and how to prevent them using cleanup functions. The core concepts involve React hooks like useState and useEffect, along with TypeScript for type safety. By the end, you'll have a functional component that safely handles API calls and avoids outdated data.
intro.usecase: Race conditions frequently occur in real-world React applications when multiple asynchronous operations compete for the same state. For example, in a dashboard with multiple filters (date range, category, status), rapid filter changes can trigger overlapping API calls where older responses overwrite newer ones, displaying incorrect data. Similarly, in e-commerce product pages with 'Add to Cart' buttons, multiple quick clicks can cause inventory mismatches if requests aren't properly sequenced. Understanding race condition fixes helps developers build reliable search interfaces, form submissions, and real-time data displays that maintain consistency regardless of user interaction timing.

objectives: Implement a cleanup function to prevent state updates on unmounted components
Apply a boolean flag to control asynchronous operations in useEffect
Construct a race condition scenario with multiple rapid API requests
Configure useEffect dependencies to manage side-effect execution
Update component state conditionally based on component mount status
Integrate abort controllers to cancel pending fetch requests
Manipulate asynchronous data fetching to ensure only the latest request completes
